title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: the continuation (pp. 650 bis–787) of La Longue Marche, where Grothendieck develops a discrete theory of 'L-groupes', i.e. groups with a loop structure ('structure à lacets'). These are combinatorial models of fundamental groups of punctured surfaces (and orbifold quotients such as PSL2(Z) ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1), with the loops around the punctures singled out. On the previous page he proposes a new presentation of an L-structure on a group Π. It consists of two data. First, a free Z-module T of rank 1, the orientation module (a discrete analogue of Z(1)). Second, a finite family (K_i)_{i∈I} of germs of exterior homomorphisms T → Π. A germ is a homomorphism nT → Π defined only on some finite-index subgroup nT, taken modulo restriction to smaller finite-index subgroups and modulo inner automorphisms of Π. This page: let Π_0 ⊂ Π be any subgroup of finite index. Each 'effective' homomorphism nT → Π in the class K_i restricts, on a smaller mT, to a homomorphism into Π_0, since some power of the image of a generator lies in Π_0. Taking these up to Π_0-conjugation gives, for fixed i, a finite set of germs of exterior homomorphisms T → Π_0. These correspond to the cusps of the covering lying over the i-th cusp. Letting i vary over the finite set I gives a finite set altogether. This is the induced structure on Π_0. The single axiom of an L-structure is then: there exists a finite-index Π_0 such that the induced structure comes from an honest loop structure on Π_0. So an L-group is a group that is virtually a surface group with its cusp loops, the cusp data being remembered only as germs, i.e. up to taking roots or powers. This handles orbifold/elliptic phenomena and cusp generators that only have roots in Π. He then generalizes, continuing on the next page: drop the finite-index requirement on Π_0 but require Π_0 to be normal. Each germ in K_i must factor through Π_0 and the induced structure must come from a loop structure on Π_0, uniquely determined once Π_0 is chosen. Π_0 is then well defined up to commensurability: if Π_0 and Π'_0 both work, so does Π_0 ∩ Π'_0. A marginal note on the next page observes that the induced set of germs need no longer be finite a priori. The aim is a commensurability-invariant (virtual) definition of loop structures, suitable for Teichmüller/mapping-class type groups in the Galois–Teichmüller program.
errors: No real error. In the finite-index case, finiteness for fixed i holds because the Π_0-classes inside a Π-class are indexed by a quotient of the finite set Π_0\Π. In the infinite-index generalization this finiteness fails, as Grothendieck himself notes in the margin of the next page. Uniqueness of the loop structure on Π_0 has to be imposed, and he does impose it.

ideas.what: Encoding a loop/cusp structure on a group Π as a finite set of germs of exterior homomorphisms from an orientation module T ≅ Z into Π, with germs taken relative to finite-index subgroups of T
ideas.modern_name: Peripheral structure (conjugacy classes of maximal cyclic/parabolic subgroups) taken up to commensurability; discrete analogue of cuspidal inertia with values in Z(1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Peripheral structures: classical 3-manifold/Kleinian group theory (Waldhausen, Thurston); Z(1)-valued inertia: Grothendieck SGA1 / Esquisse
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche and Esquisse d'un programme discuss loop/orientation structures; this germ formulation seems to be in the unpublished continuation

ideas.what: Induced structure on a finite-index subgroup (cusps of a covering lying above a cusp, given by double cosets), and the axiom 'virtually a loop structure'
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental groups / virtually surface groups with peripheral structure

ideas.what: Generalized L-structure: a normal subgroup Π_0 (possibly of infinite index), defined up to commensurability, carrying a loop structure through which the germs factor
ideas.modern_name: Groups containing a normal surface subgroup with compatible peripheral structure, e.g. Birman exact sequences π_1(S_{g,n}) → Γ_{g,n+1} → Γ_{g,n} and surface-by-X extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman (1969); later Galois–Teichmüller work (Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto) for the profinite fiber-group setting

missed.claim: A commensurability-invariant axiomatics of 'groups with loop structure' via germs of exterior homomorphisms Z → Π, extended to normal subgroups of infinite index. It is apparently meant to treat fiber-type groups (surface group inside a mapping-class-type group) uniformly. No such general formalism appears in the literature under this form.
missed.quote: On peut généraliser la notion de L-structure, en s'inspirant de la définition précédente (p. cx), et en y laissant tomber l'exigence que Π0 soit d'indice fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Related notions (peripheral structures up to commensurability, cuspidal inertia for fiber groups in anabelian geometry) are handled ad hoc. Grothendieck's germ formalism is a possible uniform framework, but its value is modest and largely anticipated by orbifold and relatively hyperbolic group theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, unpublished reformulation of Grothendieck's discrete 'groupes à lacets' via germs and commensurability. Conceptually neat, but close to standard orbifold and peripheral-structure ideas; the infinite-index generalization is only sketched.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear insertion in line 1 is probably not 'fini [?] Π_0 [?]' but something like '(pour i ...)' placed above 'trouve'. Read: 'et tout sous-groupe Π0 de Π d'indice fini, on trouve (pour i fixé) un ens. de germes d'hom. extérieurs'.
'de la classe K_i ♮ [?]' should be the decorated class symbol K_i^ξ (or K_i^♮) as on the previous page.
'dont un [?] (pour i variable) dans I' should read approximately 'donc un ens. fini pour i variable dans I'.
'l'unique [?] axiome' is correct: 'l'unique axiome d'une L-structure'.
'(p. cx)' is likely a page reference to the earlier definition.
